Let me touch briefly on Artificial Intelligence (AI). I believe it’s not AI that will replace humans — it’s the humans who learn to use AI that will replace those who don’t. 
Would you agree?

AI has its pros and cons, but what really worries me is seeing university students rely on it to do their assignments. In some countries, undergraduates have even been reported to submit AI-written work. 

I’m not entirely sure if the same is happening here in Malaysia, but it does make me wonder;
i) Is the honor code starting to crumble, or has it already fallen apart? 
ii) Are skill and real learning slowly fading away? 
iii) Are we on the brink of an academic crisis? 
iv) Has AI really become something we can’t do without, or are we just convincing ourselves that we need it?

Share your thoughts.

Politics.
📍🔥Berita terkini.o
The Bersatu Ampang Division has unanimously lost confidence in Muhyiddin Yassin’s leadership and called for his resignation as party president. According to its secretary, Daing Mohamad Daing Makati, Muhyiddin has failed to address the party’s deepening internal crisis.

Nampaknya, pergolakan dalam parti Bersatu pimpinan @MuhyiddinYassin semakin meruncing — malah boleh dikatakan sudah di tahap parah. 

Perkembangan ini sepatutnya menggembirakan PH, khususnya PKR, kerana ketidaktentuan dalam Bersatu pasti melemahkan parti itu menjelang PRN Sabah dan pilihan raya negeri lain sebelum tibanya PRU16.

Hanya satu persoalan yang masih belum terjawab — adakah kekuatan PKR kini benar-benar berada pada tahap maksimum? Apa kata #DAMAI @n_izzah, @datoramanan dan @AmirudinShari?

📍Mahathir Oh Mahathir.

July 2025: he attended the “Turun Anwar” rally at Dataran Merdeka, accusing Anwar of betraying the people’s trust, worsening the cost of living, and failing to deliver reforms. He urged Anwar to resign immediately, citing his own 2020 resignation under party pressure.

August 2025: He then questioned the validity of Anwar’s 2018 royal pardon, claiming that if it’s invalid, Anwar should step down as Prime Minister.

3 November 2025: Mahathir again took aim at Anwar, criticizing the trade deal with the US as a threat to Malaysia’s sovereignty in food, agriculture, and mining. He called the agreement’s exit clause “deceptive” and urged Anwar and his Cabinet to resign.

At this rate, will Tun M ever stop telling DS @anwaribrahim to step down?

Do you want DS Anwar to step down?

Indicate here.

🇵🇭 TYPHOON KALMAEGI FLOODS CENTRAL PHILIPPINES, KILLS 4

Typhoon Kalmaegi, locally called Tino, slammed into the Philippines, killing at least 4 people, flooding cities, and forcing tens of thousands to evacuate.

Winds hit 130 kph, with gusts up to 180 kph, as homes in Cebu were submerged and rescue boats waded through chest-deep water.

Flights were canceled, roads turned to rivers, and storm surges of up to 3 meters are still a threat.

Kalmaegi is now moving across the South China Sea, with Vietnam bracing for a second landfall - and it’s already dealing with deadly floods of its own.

Source: Reuters, @WeatherMonitors, @volcaholic1, @ChynoNews

🌏 Another Typhoon Hits the Philippines — Typhoon Kalmaegi (TinoPH) 🌊

Good afternoon everyone,

Typhoon Kalmaegi, locally named TinoPH, made landfall in southern Leyte, right in the heart of the central Philippines, bringing with it torrential rainfall and powerful gusts of wind. The storm left widespread flooding in its wake with Cebu City among the hardest-hit areas. Streets quickly turned into rivers, and dozens of vehicles and homes ended up submerged underwater.

Emergency crews have been working around the clock to help affected families, and thousands have been forced to evacuate low-lying and coastal areas as floodwaters rose rapidly. Power outages and landslides have also been reported in parts of the Visayas region, which has already endured more than its fair share of storms this year.

 A Busy Typhoon Season in the Western Pacific
As of November 4th, 2025, Typhoon Kalmaegi marks the 12th typhoon to form in the Western Pacific basin this season and the 25th named tropical storm overall. That makes it the third typhoon since September, continuing what’s been a particularly active few months for the region.

For context, the Western Pacific is the most active tropical cyclone basin on Earth, and the Philippines often finds itself directly in the firing line. Warm ocean waters fuel these systems, and with sea surface temperatures running above average this year, it’s no surprise that storms have intensified so frequently.

Meteorologists are continuing to monitor Kalmaegi’s track as it moves west-northwest it’s expected to weaken slightly as it crosses the islands, but heavy rainfall and flooding risks remain for much of the central and northern Philippines over the next 24–48 hours.

💧 A sobering reminder:
While we love to talk about our Cornish weather quirks here at KWT, from drizzle to downpours, it’s important to remember how powerful and destructive nature can be elsewhere in the world. Communities in the Philippines face these events multiple times a year, and recovery can take months, even years.

Our thoughts go out to everyone affected by Typhoon Kalmaegi and to the emergency responders working tirelessly on the ground.

Kind regards,
KWT Dave 🌦️
(Keeping an eye on the world’s weather, one storm at a time.)

Typhoon Kalmaegi (#TinoPH) has unleashed catastrophic flooding across the central Philippines, especially in Cebu province, where entire towns have been submerged. Verified footage shows cows, cars, trucks, and even shipping containers swept away by muddy floodwaters.

At least 26 people killed, with the majority of deaths reported in Cebu

Hundreds of thousands displaced, many forced to seek refuge on rooftops

Winds reached up to 155 km/h, knocking out power and blocking roads

Rainfall exceeded monthly averages in just 24 hours, overwhelming infrastructure

TRAFFIC ADVISORY

In connection with “Baba Bageshwar Dham Pad Yatra” led by Shree Dhirendra Krishna Shastri Ji on 07.11.2025 (Friday) from Adhya Katyayani Mandir, Chhattarpur to Shree Banke Bihari Mandir, Vrindavan (U.P.) from 11:00 AM onwards, a large gathering of over 50,000 devotees and vehicles is expected.

To ensure safe and smooth traffic movement, the following restrictions and diversions will remain effective in Mehrauli, South Delhi:

📍 RESTRICTED STRETCHES
* Y-Point, Chhattarpur ↔️ Dera More (SSN Marg): 11:00 AM–08:00 PM
* CDR Chowk ↔️ Y-Point, Chhattarpur: 08:00 AM–04:00 PM
* Zeer Khod ↔️ Dera More: 01:00 PM–10:00 PM (07.11.25) & 07:00 AM–01:00 PM (08.11.25)

📍 PARKING RESTRICTIONS
* No parking from CDR Chowk to Dera Mandi and Zeer Khod (08:00 AM–10:00 PM).
* Violators’ vehicles will be towed and prosecuted as per law.

📍 ALTERNATIVE ROUTES
* Towards Faridabad → MG Road via CDR Chowk
* Towards Gurugram → Mandi Road via CDR Chowk
* From Dera Gaon → Bandh Road–Mandi Road–MG Road
📍 ADVISORY
* Avoid SSN Marg, Chhattarpur Mandir Road & 100 Foota Road.
* Prefer public transport & follow police directions.
* Emergency vehicles will be given priority movement.
📍Stay updated through Delhi Traffic Police channels.

#DPTrafficAdvisory
